pl-duchy-warsaw.title: Flag of the Duchy of Warsaw

colors.note: Traditionally associated with the Polish coat of arms.

desc: - The Duchy of Warsaw (1807–1815) was a Napoleonic client state. Its flag was a white-and-crimson bicolour, establishing the Polish national colours
- **Construction:** two horizontal bands of white (top) and crimson/pink (bottom), the traditional Polish colours
trivia:
- The Duchy of Warsaw (1807–1815) was a French-aligned state
- Represented a brief period of Polish sovereignty during Napoleonic wars
- Partitioned after Napoleon's defeat

pl-november-uprising.title: Flag of the Polish November Uprising

colors.note: The White Eagle, national symbol since the 13th century.
The blood shed in the uprising against Russian rule.

desc:
- The 1831 November Uprising flag solidified white and red as the Polish national colours
- The white represented the White Eagle, red the setting sun of freedom
- **Construction:** three horizontal bands of white, blue or red, and white — variant tricolours used during the 1830–1831 uprising
trivia:
- The November Uprising (1830–1831) was a Polish revolt against Russian rule
- Represented Polish nationalism and independence aspirations
- Crushed by Russian forces but strengthened Polish identity
